summary: RelaisÉcho Link is a guided camera checkup that runs in any web browser, works offline and compares each person with their own baseline instead of a population average. A positioning outline coaches the person back into the same place as their first checkup, quality checks refuse bad light or movement, and the app estimates pulse and breathing from the camera, takes matched dental photos and runs eye and reaction checks. Results become a short packet (text, file or QR code) that a remote nurse or flight surgeon can read with no server; video never leaves the device. NASA data shows why this matters: 23 of 60 Inspiration4 blood results the day after landing were inside the lab's normal range but outside that crew member's own pre-flight values, and in NASA bed rest studies plasma volume fell a median 10.4% in the first week. With a signal delay to Mars of up to about 20 minutes each way, the comparison has to happen on the device. The same need exists on Earth in remote northern communities far from a clinic. It is a research prototype, not a diagnostic device.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

RelaisÉcho Link turns a phone or laptop camera into a careful, repeatable checkup for people far from a clinic: astronauts on long missions, and on Earth, people in remote and northern communities. Instead of judging a value against a population range, it compares each person with their own first checkup, inside a stated noise band, and shows what changed.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Line up: a ghost outline from the person's baseline coaches them back into the same framing and distance.

2. Refuse: every frame is checked for face position, light, clipping, movement and frame rate. Only good frames count, and the app says why it refuses.

3. Measure: pulse from skin colour changes (POS method, nine skin regions, 10 second windows, rejected windows reported); breathing from neck, torso and head motion; matched front and side dental photos with an automatic colour comparison; an Amsler eye grid and a tumbling E eye chart; a 3 minute reaction test (PVT-B settings); a symptom checklist with an urgent message for chest pain or shortness of breath; experimental checks (jaw opening, eye following, pupil light response, inner eyelid colour, neck photos, hand steadiness, and pulse timing and colour indexes that are never shown as mmHg or %).

4. Relay: a short packet as text, JSON, compressed file, QR code or print. The reviewer opens it in the same app with no upload, sees a "read first" list (urgent ticks, changes outside the band, low quality captures) and sends back a reply file.

5. Overview and Board: a one screen body chart with trend graphs against the person's own first values, plus mission tiles: radiation budget, space weather, signal delay to Mars, daylight by latitude, Inspiration4 crew blood data and NASA bed rest fluid shift.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Earlier, fairer detection of change for one person over time, with no wearable, account or server. It works offline after the first visit, keeps every frame on the device, and gives a remote clinician a compact, honest summary that fits a slow or expensive link.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

JavaScript (ES modules), HTML and CSS; a service worker for offline use; IndexedDB for on-device storage; MediaPipe Face Landmarker (Apache 2.0) for face landmarks; our own signal processing (filters, FFT, POS pulse, breathing tracking); Python to summarize NASA datasets; 113 unit tests, 117 headless browser checks and axe-core accessibility audits. Hosted on GitHub Pages. Open source under Apache 2.0.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It treats refusal as a feature: the app abstains rather than guessing. It compares people with themselves, uses the iris as a built-in ruler for millimetre measurements and to match the face distance of dental photos, and labels every number as LIVE, MODELED, PUBLISHED or NASA DATA, each with an Evidence button naming its source and what it cannot tell you.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Privacy (no upload, no account, an erase everything button); accuracy limits (camera pulse error is higher on darker skin in published work, and the app says so); no combined health score; language (English, a French draft, and Inuktitut left empty for a certified translator rather than machine translation); accessibility (five text sizes, light and dark, spoken coaching, screen reader checks).

STATUS

Working prototype, not yet validated on real people. Next step: a real-device bench test (pulse against a fingertip oximeter, breathing against a metronome). Not a diagnostic device.

AI USE

All creative decisions were made by the team. Claude (Anthropic) wrote the code, tests and documentation under the team's direction. ChatGPT Astra was also used. The logo was generated with ChatGPT. Details: AI_DISCLOSURE.md in the repository.
